newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm, Brent bounces with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm, Brent bounces with NYMEX.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed firmer on Thursday, pulled higher by bouncing Brent crude which shrugged off mildly bearish U.S. inventory data to rally to new session highs by late afternoon, brokers said.
June IPE gas oil closed $1.25 firmer at $174.50 a tonne as Brent drew encouragement from a technical rally in New York markets, they said.
"It's basically WTI (NYMEX) crude which seems to be the leader at the moment," said a broker.
"The break through $21.00 (a barrel) triggered a few buy-stops," he added.

July Brent crude was trading up 35 cents at $19.59 a barrel by 1700 GMT, just four cents below the intraday high posted moments earlier and well above the session low of $19.10 posted in early afternoon trade.
Dealers said Brent's break above Wednesday's high of $19.34 and through resistance at $19.43 generated further momentum of its own but a barrier at $19.65 appeared to be holding.
Lght short-covering reversed early afternoon losses posted on the back of the release of U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) data showing crude and gasoline stocks rose last week, they said.

DOE figures showed U.S. crude stocks rose 3.2 million barrels last week. The DOE also reported a 1.1 million rise in gasoline stocks, the exact reverse of American Petroleum Institute (API) data released on Tuesday.
"Post API days usually produce a reversal if the initial reaction to the inventory numbers loses momentum in the first hour or so," said Charles Gray of brokers Prudential Bache.
